newsitem.title: UK: Dow recovery helps shares, markets await Fed.
newsitem.headline: Dow recovery helps shares, markets await Fed.

text.p: European bourses recovered their composure on Tuesday after a sharp overnight rebound on Wall Street, which climbed back from an early 50-point loss to close up slightly.
London, Frankfurt and Paris, which all closed well down on Monday -- with London suffering its biggest drop in two months -- all opened higher on Tuesday, though London fell back later.
The Dow ended up 6.28 points at a record 5,894.74.
But stock and currency markets were effectively holding their breath on Tuesday ahead of a crucial U.S. monetary policy-making meeting.

Dealers and analysts were deeply divided over whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) committee would sanction a credit tightening after the meeting (at 1300 gmt), the outcome of which would not be known until after European trading wound down. If the Fed decided to increase interest rates, it would be the first rise for 1-1/2 years.

Despite its higher open, London's blue chip FTSE 100 index later retreated into negative ground on profit-taking by institutional investors. But traders said volume remained thin as the market awaited news from a regular British monetary policy conclave on Monday, as well as the Fed meeting.
"It's going to be an interesting day," said one senior trader. "Most people will probably be sidelined, we have a powerful coincidence of events creating a powerful reason for people to stand aside."
Yet some still believed the FTSE was on track to breach the 4,000 level it failed to attain in a record-breaking run last week.
In Frankfurt, German shares opened firmer following the Dow's gains in pre-bourse electronic exchanges and also began floor trade about a third of a percentage point up .
And on the Paris bourse stocks also opened higher buoyed by Wall Street.
On the currency front too, the mood was one of wait and see. The dollar was a touch softer early in Europe and traders said the markets were treading water awaiting the FOMC
The consensus forecast among those who expected a rate rise was for a 25 basis-point (quarter percent) increase. That was now priced into the market, dealers said.
The dollar was at 1.5117 marks and 109.78 yen compared with 1.5120 marks and 109.88 yen in Europe late on Monday.
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 7.4 points down at 3,912.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 15.65 points up at 2,082.74.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 10.08 at 2,637.12. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed firmer at $381.60 compared with Monday's London Gold close of $381.25. Silver was also firmer at $4.90 cents.
